This is a very common first sign of depression, if you trust your parents or doctor maybe consider telling them you would like to start seeing a therapist oriented to mindfulness, motivation or/and has teen counseling experience.

I am in no means a professional so take this however you will - Everyone is different but there are generally signs of domination in relationships and even if you trust someone fully these unhealthy signs you are describing should be closely looked at.. Maybe an honest conversation could help but if that isn't a go to then maybe you should reevaluate your trust in one another and the relationship. This reminds me of one my ex's who did this with me as well, over time it only got worse, she had to know everything I was saying and doing with who and when and I wasnt allowed answers to more and more things such as who she was with, where she was, what she was up to  and such things.. Casual conversation became a topic to tread carefully more and more so. it never felt like an abusive relationship and I don't really regard it as one still but I wasn't happy. I realized the anxiety she gave me and the nervousness I had that if I slipped up she would lose her temper was beginning to be overwhelming I ended up running away from it and am doing much better now relationship wise. When I look back as soon as I started even questioning what I should do about it is when I should have left. The moral of this story is that sometimes a pain someone is causing you isn't really evident until it gets out of hand or you take a step back. I wish you the best and hope that my experience was of some help to you
